source.title: Refinement Buys Intelligibility, Search Buys Identity: What Test-Time Compute Buys in Masked-Diffusion TTS
source.authors: Nityanand Mathur; H. Sayed; Ayush Singh

record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling-form and extrapolation claims in masked-diffusion TTS, and reports that fit quality, exponent contrasts, and extrapolation depend on metric, fit window, and error coordinate.
record.gate_note: The study measures validation loss across its width-depth grid and fits scaling surfaces to TTS WER and speaker similarity. It does not test language-model pretraining loss across token or compute scales, nor parameter-token compute-optimal allocation. Other reported results about search, prompt length, guidance, and codebook-level step allocation do not directly test the listed versions.
record.test_reason: A new setting (masked-diffusion codec TTS). Its own results bear on V4, through validation loss across iso-N width–depth shapes, and on V6, through small-to-large parameter-budget extrapolation of TTS error metrics. Most of the paper concerns inference-time refinement-step scaling of task errors, a different construct recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right but misses the lead result. Against measured floors, refinement from T=1 to T=16 closes 86.2% of reachable intelligibility range but 46.4% of identity range (1.86×). The ratio is stable under reparameterisation and attenuates with more training (1.84→1.23×) without reversing, so the authors report the ordering, not the factor. The pre-registered Δτ=0.110 is coordinate- and window-dependent, and the fit is rejected by χ², so they do not build on it. At matched NFE, best-of-K search buys identity where refinement cannot. Depth and steps do not exchange at a fixed rate. Shape matters for error at fixed N, but the width exponent is not identified. WER does not extrapolate from small budgets while SIM-o does. 62% of the identity gap is the codec's.
record.recipe_differences: Applies a width-depth-refinement-step scaling analysis to masked-diffusion codec TTS, using validation loss and TTS outcome metrics rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling in parameters, tokens, and compute.
record.method_sensitivity: Exponent contrast changes sign under non-affine error reparameterisations and shrinks over wider T fit windows; extrapolation differs by metric. The authors also report that resampling fit weights widens the ∆τ interval.

fits_no_version.finding: At approximately fixed N, shape strongly changes WER (40.2, 16.3 and 7.3 WER points from shallowest shape to best depth). The two-axis model beats N-only (ΔAICc −15.5 WER, −5.5 SIM-o), while validation loss moves about 1%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shape at fixed parameter count can matter strongly for downstream metrics even when loss changes only slightly.

fits_no_version.finding: Power-law exponents of TTS error against inference refinement steps depend on error coordinate and fit window. The Δτ sign flips under log, sqrt and capped maps, and Δτ halves as the T window doubles. The separable surface is rejected by χ²/dof (14.3, 8.8), and a depth–step substitution form fits worse (ΔAICc +69.3/+71.3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Test-time compute scaling exponents are coordinate- and window-dependent and do not follow a single power law.

record.peer_reviewed: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026), Workshop: Diffusion Language Models: Foundations, Efficiency, and Reasoning
record.problems: The study covers one language, codec, and corpus; models are described as under-trained; width and substitution parameters hit fit bounds; the declared fit is rejected by its own weighted criterion; the ∆τ interval widens when fit weights are resampled. The validation-loss table gives no uncertainty and uses approximate rather than exact iso-parameter budgets.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed per-config WER and SIM-o values at T=16, additional retraining and recognizer checks, and inference interventions were not included because they do not directly measure the listed loss, allocation, or fit-dependence versions. The per-layer latency allocation result concerns depth versus refinement steps, not parameter-token compute-optimal allocation.

untested.parts: All: no power-law fit of held-out loss against parameters, tokens or compute.
All: extrapolation is tested on task metrics only, not on loss.
Architecture details other than width/depth. Exactly matched N. Converged models: all runs are 30k steps and the authors say they are under-trained.
The study does not fit a loss power law in training scale for speech; its power-law fits are over inference steps and task errors.
The relation of downstream metrics to pretraining loss is not analysed. Scale spans only 20–125M across three budgets.
Fit-dependence of training-scaling exponents or of the compute-optimal split is not tested. Coordinate and window dependence is shown only for inference-step exponents.

missing.what: Training-compute scaling of SIM-o on one config (30k→90k→180k steps: 0.4081→0.4807→0.4962). Log-linear extrapolation predicts 0.5264 against 0.4962 observed: decelerating, overpredicted.
missing.locator: Section 4.4, 'Training compute is the largest identity lever'

missing.what: A fourth budget (276M) and the H-E4b result 'predicted vs observed within 15%', refuted. The extrapolation numbers are not detailed in the text. Also SIM-o gain of +0.0531 from 20M to 276M.
Per-config WER and SIM-o at T=16 beside validation loss. Needed to compare loss against downstream metrics; declared left out but relevant to V6's loss–downstream link.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V5 and V7 links rest on inference-step scaling of task error, not training-scale scaling laws, so they were relinked to none. The V4 evidence is a table the authors never analyse. Models are under-trained (30k steps), and N is only approximately matched (113–133M in budget C). The V6 extrapolation spans just three budgets over about 6× in N. The V6 verdicts treat WER and SIM-o as the TTS model's downstream tasks. The R25 affine-check Δτ of 0.0351 differs from 0.110 despite affine invariance, which hints at bound or weight-floor effects in the fits.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law test of held-out pretraining loss across parameters, training tokens, or compute.
The small-to-large extrapolation test predicts TTS WER and SIM-o, not held-out pretraining loss.
No fixed-compute optimization of parameter and token counts. The paper's depth-versus-refinement-step comparison is not the parameter-token allocation in this version.

The validation-loss grid uses approximately iso-parameter budgets rather than exactly matched parameter counts; it tests the sampled width-depth shapes, not a wide range of other architecture choices.
Tests speech TTS, but not image or video models, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer. The fitted outputs are WER and SIM-o, not pretraining loss.
No downstream task performance is related to pretraining loss or scale.
Tests dependence on error coordinate, fit window, fitting criterion, weighting, and training budget in this TTS setup; does not test parameter-counting choices or variation across datasets.
